source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
Fusarium wilt, known as Panama disease (ជម្ងឺប៉ូស), is a soil-borne fungal disease that blocks the plant's internal water-conducting tissue. Infected plants show yellowing that starts at the older, lower leaves and progresses upward, with leaves eventually collapsing and hanging down the stem; a cut through the infected pseudostem or corm reveals discolored, streaked internal tissue.

There is no effective cure once a plant is infected, and the pathogen persists in the soil for years, so management is almost entirely preventive: avoid moving soil or planting material from infected fields, remove and destroy (rather than compost) infected plants, and avoid replanting banana in a known infected site for an extended period. This is consistent with why healthy, disease-free planting material (see the propagation and corm-selection guidance) matters so much for banana growers.
